items.text: The Twins run along a damaged corridor, followed by the visitor and the repurposed Belyash.

items.speaker: Left
items.text: The power control room is up this staircase. We must travel another 80 meters forward, turn left, and then reach the room at the end of the corridor.

items.speaker: Left
items.text: Our present speed may not be sufficient given the threat Maxim poses to the facility. Comrade, would you allow me to carry you?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: *panting* If that's what's needed.
The sleek robot bends down to scoop the visitor into her arms and then launches into a forward sprint.
A crash of scraping metal thunders above them.

items.speaker: Left
items.text: Structural failure imminent. Please, brace for impact.

items.speaker: Left
items.text: The sudden lockdown of that doorway is unlikely to have been accidental. Maxim may be aware of our approach.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: *cough*

items.speaker: Left
items.text: Comrade Doctor, are you hurt?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: *cough* I'm fine. It's only the dust.

items.speaker: Left
items.text: Apologies, comrade. I will attempt to warn you should I perform a slide of that nature in the future.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: It's quite alright. Let's just keep moving.
There's another thundering sound above them, but this one is different, like heavy footsteps.

items.speaker: Right
items.text: Warning: large heat signature approaching from above.
A heavily armed Belyash drops down through the ceiling.
Right stands in front of Left, shielding their companion from the debris.

items.speaker: Left
items.text: Scanning ... Heavy firepower detected. Another Belyash variant adapted by Maxim.

items.speaker: Left
items.text: Defensive matrixes engaged.
A temporary lab has been built in the corner of the assembly shop.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: We have two unused THOUGHT Devices to examine before we poke around in anyone's head.

items.speaker: Char-les
items.text: Let me see them.
P-3 reaches out his gloved hand toward Mesmer Jr. so Char-les can interact with the THOUGHT Devices directly.

items.speaker: Char-les
items.text: Hmm. This device appears to be around three grams heavier than its technical specifications.

items.speaker: P-3
items.text: Go on then. Let's poke around inside.

items.speaker: Char-les
items.text: As you say, Major.
Char-les's tentacles inspect the device and find a narrow gap between the shell and the plate.
*click* The shell splits open.

items.speaker: Char-les
items.text: That is unusual.
Char-les raises the shell with two tentacles, displaying its insides to the others.

items.speaker: Char-les
items.text: This residue shouldn't be here.

items.speaker: X
items.text: Hmm, I do believe we've discovered our smoking gun.

items.speaker: P-3
items.text: So, what is it?

items.speaker: X
items.text: See that? Something broke apart when we opened it up, spilling out this gunk.

items.speaker: Char-les
items.text: Allow me to conduct a quick analysis. Hmm. It's a synthetic compound, a dissolving capsule made of polymer-soluble material with a biogel inside.

items.speaker: Char-les
items.text: Oh, I understand now.

items.speaker: P-3
items.text: Understand what? Enough with the suspense!

items.speaker: Char-les
items.text: Simply put, I believe Maxim inserted a capsule of polymer-soluble material into these THOUGHT Devices.

items.speaker: Char-les
items.text: Once it makes contact with the user's own polymer, the capsule begins to degrade, breaking with time or pressure until it releases its contents directly into their bloodstream.

items.speaker: P-3
items.text: Make it simple for me, Chuck.

items.speaker: Char-les
items.text: It's a poisonous time bomb.

items.speaker: P-3
items.text: So, when it goes off, it shoots a crazy pill straight into their brains?

items.speaker: Char-les
items.text: We'll need to do further tests to determine its full effects, but it's possible that the toxin may ultimately be fatal.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: We don't have time for empty speculation, gentlemen. May I take a look?
Their investigation continues.
P-3 stands tapping his foot, impatiently craning his neck away from the operation table. He's been reduced from soldier to Char-les's glorified lab chair.

items.speaker: P-3
items.text: We done yet? I'm getting a cramp standing like this.

items.speaker: Char-les
items.text: Almost. Hold me higher. I can't see the screen.

items.speaker: P-3
items.text: Yeah, yeah. What'd I do to deserve this? I should be out there smashing heads.

items.speaker: Char-les
items.text: You are a vital asset to this operation, Major. I couldn't have done this without you.

items.speaker: P-3
items.text: Aww gee. You're gonna make me tear up, Char-les.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: I think I've isolated the substance. Do you recognize this molecular structure, X?

items.speaker: X
items.text: No. It could be that this molecular structure is unique to the science of this world. Maybe we can preserve a sample for study back at Laplace.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: You do understand your life may depend on this, don't you?

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: Is there a chemist here? We're having trouble identifying this substance.

items.speaker: Ethan Brown
items.text: I can help! I have a doctorate in medicinal biochemistry.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: You did seem to be an expert in intoxicants. Have you sobered up yet?

items.speaker: Ethan Brown
items.text: Call me a drunk if you like, but I'm a drunk that got invited to this international summit. Now show me the damned report.

items.speaker: Ethan Brown
items.text: Hmm, I thought you said you were scientists? This one is almost trivial. Even a high schooler could identify it.

items.speaker: Ethan Brown
items.text: Oh, but this is a tricky one! Hmm. Its structure looks similar to adamantane.

items.speaker: Ethan Brown
items.text: It's a novel kind of synthetic neurotoxin. Quite brilliant, in fact. Maxim could have gotten a patent certificate from the Discovery and Invention Committee.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: Focus, please. You're all in serious danger.

items.speaker: Ethan Brown
items.text: I can make a list of compounds that may help neutralize the toxin, but there's no way to guarantee anything.

items.speaker: Ethan Brown
items.text: In an ideal clinical environment, we would run trials to determine effective antidotes. Are there any lab animals here?

items.speaker: X
items.text: *sigh* If only we'd invited Medicine Pocket along.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: I doubt we'll be able to find any living animals here. We'll have to test the reactivity on blood samples. Maybe we can collect it from the scientists that have died?

items.speaker: Char-les
items.text: I would advise against that. There are too many variables in testing blood from deceased subjects. We need living cellular tissue.

items.speaker: P-3
items.text: Hold on a minute. Isn't there an obvious fix for all of this?

items.speaker: Char-les
items.text: Major, I assure you if there were, we would have thought of it before now.

items.speaker: P-3
items.text: Hear me out. Why don't we just rip these things off of everyone's head before they can release the poison?

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: Absolutely not.

items.speaker: X
items.text: Maxim accounted for that particular possibility, unfortunately. The capsule is purposefully fragile. Once it's been connected, any kind of tampering with the device is likely to break it early.

items.speaker: X
items.text: It's an ingenious trap.

items.speaker: Char-les
items.text: You see, Major. It's too risky. We could end up hastening their descent into madness rather than saving them.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: Simply put, we'd do more harm than good.

items.speaker: P-3
items.text: Okay, got it. Just figured I'd make sure we weren't missing the obvious.

items.speaker: P-3
items.text: Now what? Do we just hope no one dies between now and whenever we can round up some guinea pigs?

items.speaker: X
items.text: Actually, Major, you might just have inspired me. In absentia of any cavia porcellus, we do have the next best thing.
Mesmer shoots a sudden frown at X, already guessing at his plan.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: You're crazy.

items.speaker: X
items.text: We extract a reduced dosage of the neurotoxin and inject it into me. Then we test out the antidotes systematically until one works.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: *sigh* You already sound insane.
